about: The era registry (docs/data-plan.md, section 1). An era is a period in one environment in which nothing that affects play changed. Eras before build stamps are defined by environment and UTC window (from inclusive, to exclusive; to null while the era runs), plus layout and mindVersion (null: the facts carry none); stamped eras by `build` (set at deploy by scripts/deploy.mjs as <env>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<short sha>[-dirty]). At each deploy: close the running era of that environment (`to`), and add or fill the new one (`build`, `from`, worker, commits). Predictions are judged by scripts/era-report.mjs against the era's `baseline` (see scripts/lib/eras.mjs for the measures and verdict rules). Times come from `wrangler deployments list`.

eras.change: The lighter Jev (L4, mindVersion 6): a bot decides only at decision moments (it spawns, its goal ends or fails, the case changes state, or 10 s pass) and holds its goal in between; Jev is asked at those moments, never within 3 s of the last request; each decision also sets a stance, fight or focus (ignore rats unless they block the way or shoot). Every decision moment is recorded with its stance. About 1 round in 5 is a code-only round: the bots keep the code mind even with humans playing, to measure what Jev is worth. Ships with protocol 25 (Tyler, 30 September): Closing Time dropped (three modes), Blackout with a hard flashlight beam on every rat, heavy Big Cheese (one shot per second, damage 2 plus one per size step); also supply claim juice with heavy Ironclad sounds, and the reconnect fixes (supply sites no longer doubled, the restored rat turns with the camera).

eras.change: Case grip, calmer bot aim and bot archetypes (Tyler, 1 October): a carried case is knocked loose by 3 enemy balls each within 2 s of the last (it was one ball); killing the carrier still drops it. Perf reports carry ping and how far behind other rats are drawn (measurement only). Excessive Force stays at 10 kills; no time limits, ever. Protocol 26 adds: archetypes dealt evenly per room; PAPER CHASE to 5 deliveries; Jurisdiction zones hold 20 points that drain only while the case is held there, then move; a shot case flies 20% slower; taking the case brings a random supply (once per 20 s per rat); the case rebuilt and made juicy (K1, K2, new sounds); loose-spell and drop-cause recording.
eras.notes: Tyler's target: Excessive Force averages 15–20 minutes, the longest mode but not by much (it was 27.5 minutes over 45 rounds from 29 September to 1 October, bot-only rounds included). If Paper Chase or Jurisdiction get too short, raise their targets. Bot-only rounds count: the city runs them all day. Paper Chase and Jurisdiction changed rules in this era, so their round lengths are a new baseline, not a prediction. Loose-spell measures (case.looseMedianS, loosePathMedian, looseKicksMean) start here; the earlier eras have none.
